preview_en:
AC Milan look to bounce back from their recent winless slump when they host a Lecce side who haven’t won a Serie A H2H at San Siro in nearly three decades.

Match News and Current Form

Milan opened their UEFA Europa League campaign with a 2-0 defeat to Benfica in their first league phase game on Wednesday, handing Ruben Amorim his first competitive defeat in charge. The Rossoneri are winless in their last three games (D2, L1), and with both draws coming in Serie A, they could now post three consecutive stalemates in the competition for the first time since September 2018. Returning to the San Siro isn’t necessarily the positive omen it may seem in ending that streak for Milan, who have lost four of their last six competitive games here (W1, D1), and though that sole win came in their last league outing here, they’ve managed consecutive home Serie A wins only once this calendar year.

Lecce edged Monza 3-2 last Sunday to bounce back from consecutive defeats to nil, but this trip appears fraught with danger for a side whose only two wins this season came against newly-promoted sides. Those victories ensure they occupy a mid-table position ahead of this round, but achieving great consistency is likely to be key in ensuring they don’t find themselves in a relegation battle this term as the Salentians won consecutive league games just twice last season. Picking up their first set of back-to-back wins this season seems a possibility here having won three of their last four away league games (D1).

Head-to-Head History

Milan have won the last five Serie A H2Hs and could post six consecutive victories in this fixture for the first time in the competition. Lecce haven’t won a competitive H2H since April 2006, while their last away H2H victory dates back to October 1997.

Hot Stats and Streaks

All seven of Milan’s league goals this season arrived after the hour mark.

Eight of Milan’s last ten home league wins came by a single-goal margin.

Lecce have conceded seven of their last ten Serie A goals within the first 30 minutes.

Only five of Lecce’s last 17 away league games saw both teams score.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Diego Moreira could continue Milan’s late goal trend as his last four personal strikes have come in the second half, including a brace against Lazio in the Rossoneri’s latest league game. Lassana Coulibaly could precede him on the scoresheet as his last six Serie A goals arrived before half-time, five of which opened the scoring.

Neither side seem to have any new injury scares.

Betting Analysis

A goalless first-half could be on the cards as both these teams have struggled to score before the break this season.

Author: Sridhar Bhamidi
